name: Planet spectra as molecular spectroscopy
summary: Identifying planetary atmospheric species relies on laboratory rovibrational line lists and selection rules; the same spectroscopy underlies remote sensing of planets and exoplanets.

name: Planetary climate as Earth climate physics
summary: Energy balance, greenhouse effect and feedbacks developed for Earth apply to other planets and exoplanets, setting equilibrium temperatures and habitability.

name: Physical limits of life and biosignatures
summary: Habitability asks which physical constraints (energy, chemistry, thermodynamics) permit life; physics of living systems quantifies those limits, such as energy use, noise and information processing.

name: Habitable zone from climate feedbacks
summary: Habitable-zone edges are set by radiative-convective climate physics: runaway greenhouse from water-vapour feedback and ice-albedo snowball transitions, as in Earth climate models.

name: Transmission spectra as molecular absorption
summary: Exoplanet transmission and emission spectra are decoded using molecular line lists, cross sections and Raman/collision-induced absorption knowledge from molecular spectroscopy.

name: Radiative transfer codes from Earth to exoplanets
summary: Radiative-convective models, correlated-k opacities and general circulation models built for Earth climate are reused for exoplanet atmospheres and retrievals.
breaks: Earth-tuned assumptions (water condensation, near-1 bar) fail for hot Jupiters and non-solar compositions.

name: Spectroscopic databases serve exoplanet retrievals
summary: Line lists such as HITRAN and ExoMol, from quantum-chemistry and spectroscopy, are essential inputs for interpreting JWST exoplanet spectra.

name: Greenhouse and inversion physics on other worlds
summary: Greenhouse trapping, lapse rates and temperature inversions explain exoplanet thermal structure just as they do Earth's atmosphere.

name: Blackbody radiation and radiative equilibrium
summary: Both rest on Planck blackbody radiation and radiative transfer: the CMB is a relic thermal spectrum, Earth's climate set by balance of absorbed sunlight and outgoing thermal radiation.
breaks: The CMB is a decoupled relic freely streaming; Earth's emission is non-equilibrium and gray-body with strong absorption bands.

name: Convection and radiative-convective structure
summary: Stellar envelopes and planetary atmospheres share Schwarzschild/lapse-rate stability criteria and mixing-length convection; the adiabatic gradient decides radiative versus convective layers.
breaks: Stars have radiation pressure, ionization and nuclear sources; atmospheres have moisture and rotation constraints.

name: Helioseismology and seismology inversions
summary: Both infer interior structure from observed wave modes and travel times via inversion: p-modes for the Sun, body and surface waves and normal modes for Earth. Methods and the mathematics of tomography parallel each other.
breaks: Solar modes are stochastically excited acoustic waves in a fluid; Earth has shear waves, discontinuities and sparse source locations.

name: Neutron-star asteroseismology and crust elasticity
summary: Neutron-star crusts support shear modes and quakes analogous to earthquakes; magnetar giant-flare quasi-periodic oscillations are interpreted as crustal torsional modes, as in seismology.
breaks: Crust is a Coulomb lattice at nuclear densities with extreme magnetic fields and superfluid coupling.

name: Solar forcing of climate
summary: Solar luminosity, its variability and the faint young Sun set the incoming flux in Earth's energy balance; solar cycle irradiance variations give a small forcing term.

name: Dynamo theory: Sun and geodynamo
summary: Solar and geodynamo both arise from MHD induction in convecting conducting fluid, with rotation and helicity (alpha-omega effect) driving field generation and reversals.
breaks: Solar dynamo is turbulent with strong stratification and a 11-yr cycle; geodynamo has low Rossby number and the solid inner core.

name: Rossby waves and density waves
summary: Both feature large-scale rotating-fluid wave patterns: Rossby waves from the beta effect in atmospheres, and spiral density waves in rotating galactic disks with differential rotation, with analogous dispersion structure.
breaks: Galactic disks are self-gravitating and collisionless stars; Rossby waves are restoring-force vorticity waves in a fluid.

name: Rotating stratified turbulence in disks and atmospheres
summary: Protoplanetary-disk vortices, zonal flows and Rossby wave instability parallel geophysical vortices and jets in rotating shear flows; Coriolis dynamics governs both.
breaks: Disks involve magnetorotational turbulence, dust coupling and self-gravity.

name: Cosmic-ray and hadron-therapy interactions
summary: Heavy-ion transport, nuclear fragmentation and Bragg-peak energy loss are shared: galactic cosmic-ray shielding for astronauts uses the same codes and radiobiology as carbon-ion therapy.

name: Cosmic accelerators versus machines
summary: Diffusive shock acceleration and Fermi mechanisms are natural counterparts of laboratory accelerators; the Hillas criterion parallels the size-times-field limit on achievable energy.
breaks: Cosmic acceleration is stochastic, shock-based and power-law; machines use coherent, controlled RF fields.

name: Synchrotron radiation in nature and the lab
summary: Relativistic electrons in magnetic fields emit synchrotron radiation, identical physics in AGN jets, pulsar nebulae and storage-ring light sources, with the same critical-frequency scaling.

name: Jets and undulator radiation
summary: Relativistic jets emit synchrotron and inverse-Compton radiation, with Doppler boosting; undulators and FELs give coherent, narrow-band versions of the same radiation by accelerated charges.
breaks: Jet emission is incoherent and broadband; FELs achieve coherence via microbunching.

name: Coherent emission from bunched charges
summary: FRB models invoke coherent curvature or maser emission from bunched charges, resembling coherent synchrotron radiation and FEL microbunching where power scales as N².
breaks: FRB coherence mechanism is unsettled; FELs rely on a known collective instability.

name: Quantum sensors for dark matter
summary: Axion and light dark-matter searches use SQUIDs, atomic magnetometers, NV centres, atomic clocks and interferometers; quantum-sensing techniques set sensitivity, including squeezing.

name: Low-background detectors and scintillation
summary: Scintillators, liquid xenon and time-of-flight photodetection developed for particle and dark-matter detection also drive PET detector design; low-noise photosensors cross over.
breaks: Dark-matter detectors require extreme radiopurity and keV thresholds; PET needs high rate at 511 keV.

name: Inverse problems and tomographic reconstruction
summary: Weak-lensing mass maps and CT/MRI reconstruction are regularized linear inverse problems, using Kaiser–Squires-type inversion, Wiener filtering and sparsity priors.
breaks: Lensing has sparse noisy sampling and shape noise; CT has controlled acquisition geometry.

name: Positron annihilation and gamma detection
summary: Positron annihilation producing 511 keV photons is used in PET and is observed in the Galactic 511 keV line; gamma-ray instrumentation overlaps with nuclear-medicine detectors, such as Compton cameras.

name: Statistical inference of dynamical systems
summary: Galactic archaeology and biophysical data analysis both use Bayesian inference and machine learning on large noisy catalogues; Gaia phase-space modelling parallels inference in living-systems data.
breaks: The shared element is generic statistical practice.

name: Cosmic rays and air showers in the atmosphere
summary: Cosmic rays are detected through extensive air showers developing in the atmosphere; cosmic-ray ionisation is also proposed to affect atmospheric electricity and cloud nucleation.
breaks: Cosmic-ray cloud seeding is weak and disputed.

name: Milankovitch cycles and orbital forcing
summary: Secular orbital perturbations change Earth's eccentricity, obliquity and precession, modulating insolation and driving glacial cycles.
breaks: Climate response is nonlinear, with ice-sheet feedbacks.

name: Astrochemistry in disks
summary: Disk chemistry and the delivery of volatiles depend on gas-phase and grain-surface reaction rates, ion-molecule kinetics and snow lines, drawing on reaction-dynamics rate theory.

name: Grain-surface chemistry and catalysis
summary: H2 formation and ice mantle chemistry on dust grains proceed via adsorption, diffusion and Langmuir–Hinshelwood reactions, the same surface-science mechanisms as in heterogeneous catalysis.
breaks: Interstellar grains are at ~10 K with quantum tunnelling, in ultra-low-density gas.

name: Opacities and equations of state
summary: Stellar and planetary interiors require atomic opacities and equations of state computed with electronic-structure methods, including density functional and molecular dynamics for warm dense matter.
breaks: Stellar plasmas are partially ionized at high temperature, beyond standard ground-state quantum chemistry.

name: Turbulence in stratified fluids
summary: Intracluster gas and the oceans are stratified turbulent fluids, with buoyancy-driven mixing and internal gravity waves described by Brunt–Väisälä frequency.
breaks: Cluster gas is magnetized, weakly collisional plasma with cooling and AGN feedback.
